- **Checks:** [`test_c1_signal_event_failure`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c1_process_interaction.py)
- **Taught on:** [Signal event failure](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/tasks-and-processes/#wait-signals-and-child-flows)

**Start and wait for a process**: A task starts a child flow, such as an inspection, and waits until it ends.

API details

- **SimPy:** `yield env.process(child())`
- **YAML:** `wait: {task: inspect}`
- **Builder:** `wait={"task": "inspect"}`, or `yield context.call("inspect")`
- **Low-level:** `yield env.process(child())`
- **Checks:** [`test_c1_start_and_wait_for_a_process`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c1_process_interaction.py)
- **Taught on:** [Start and wait for a process](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/tasks-and-processes/#wait-signals-and-child-flows)

**Process return value**: The task that waited for a child flow reads what the child produced.

API details

- **SimPy:** a process's `return` value
- **YAML:** `wait.inspect.value.<field>`, the last payload of the child flow
- **Builder:** the same, or the value of `context.call(...)`
- **Low-level:** `value = yield env.process(child())`
- **Checks:** [`test_c1_process_return_value`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c1_process_interaction.py)
- **Taught on:** [Process return value](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/tasks-and-processes/#wait-signals-and-child-flows)

**Process failure**: A failure inside a child flow reaches the task waiting for it, which can handle it or fail in turn.

API details

- **SimPy:** an exception raised in a process reaches the process that waits for it
- **YAML:** `fail`, `fail_reason` and `on_fail` on a task; a failure no `on_fail` handles fails the waiting task
- **Builder:** the same, and a function that raises fails its task
- **Low-level:** `try: yield env.process(child())` and `except`
- **Checks:** [`test_c1_process_failure`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c1_process_interaction.py), [`test_c1_process_failure_handled_by_on_fail`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c1_process_interaction.py)
- **Difference:** In YAML and the builder a failure no task waits for ends the entity's flow, publishes `failed` and is counted, and the run goes on; in SimPy, and in the low-level API, an exception nobody handles stops the run.
- **Taught on:** [Process failure](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/tasks-and-processes/#wait-signals-and-child-flows)

**Event inspection**: A condition reads whether a signal has fired, whether it succeeded, and its value.

API details

- **SimPy:** `Event.triggered`, `.processed`, `.ok`, `.value`
- **YAML:** `signal.<name>.count`, `.ok` and `.value` in a condition
- **Builder:** `context.signal(name).wait()` and its SimPy attributes, or the signal's `count`, `ok` and `value`
- **Low-level:** the same attributes of SimPy events and `Signal`
- **Checks:** [`test_c1_event_inspection`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c1_process_interaction.py)
- **Taught on:** [Event inspection](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/tasks-and-processes/#wait-signals-and-child-flows)

**Process inspection**: After a wait, a task reads whether a child flow has finished, whether it succeeded, and its value.

API details

- **SimPy:** `Process.is_alive`, `.triggered`, `.ok`, `.value`
- **YAML:** `wait.<branch>.done`, `.ok` and `.value` after the wait
- **Builder:** the process `context.spawn` and `context.call` return
- **Low-level:** the process `env.process` returns
- **Checks:** [`test_c1_process_inspection`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c1_process_interaction.py)
- **Taught on:** [Process inspection](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/tasks-and-processes/#wait-signals-and-child-flows)

**Wait for a shared condition**: A task waits until a condition on the model's state holds, such as stock reaching 5.

API details

- **SimPy:** a loop over a fresh "changed" event
- **YAML:** `wait: {condition: level.stock >= 5}`
- **Builder:** `wait={"condition": "level.stock >= 5"}`
- **Low-level:** `env.watch_changes(check)`, or a SimPy loop
- **Checks:** [`test_c1_wait_for_a_shared_condition`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c1_process_interaction.py)
- **Taught on:** [Wait for a shared condition](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/tasks-and-processes/#wait-signals-and-child-flows)

## C2: Wait for One or All

Waiting for the first of several events, or for all of them, as SimPy's `AnyOf` and `AllOf` conditions do.

**Wait for one event**: A task waits for whichever of several events happens first, such as a delivery or a time limit.

API details

- **SimPy:** `simpy.events.AnyOf`, `a | b`
- **YAML:** `wait: {any: {stock: {signal: restocked}, limit: {timeout: 3}}}`
- **Builder:** `wait={"any": {...}}`
- **Low-level:** `yield a | b`
- **Checks:** [`test_c2_wait_for_one_event`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c2_wait_for_one_or_all.py), [`test_c2_wait_for_one_event_two_at_one_instant`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c2_wait_for_one_or_all.py)
- **Difference:** Losing signal, timeout and condition branches are dropped when the wait ends; losing child flows keep running, as SimPy leaves processes running.
- **Taught on:** [Wait for one event](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/guides/wait-for-one-or-all/#wait-for-the-first)

**Wait for all events**: A task waits until every one of several events has happened.

API details

- **SimPy:** `simpy.events.AllOf`, `a & b`
- **YAML:** `wait: {all: {...}}`
- **Builder:** `wait={"all": {...}}`
- **Low-level:** `yield a & b`
- **Checks:** [`test_c2_wait_for_all_events`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c2_wait_for_one_or_all.py), [`test_c2_wait_for_all_events_with_a_failing_branch`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c2_wait_for_one_or_all.py)
- **Taught on:** [Wait for all events](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/guides/wait-for-one-or-all/#wait-for-all)

## C3: Interrupts and Preemption

Interrupting a task while it waits or while it is in service, and a higher-priority request taking a resource unit from a lower-priority user.

**Interrupt while waiting**: Another task or a scenario step interrupts a task while it is still in a queue.

API details

- **SimPy:** `simpy.Process.interrupt` while the process waits for a request
- **YAML:** `interrupt: {task: waiter}` on a scenario step or a task; `on_interrupt` on the task
- **Builder:** `context.interrupt("waiter")`; `@app.task(on_interrupt=...)`
- **Low-level:** `process.interrupt(cause)`, caught as `simpy.Interrupt`
- **Checks:** [`test_c3_interrupt_while_waiting`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c3_interrupts.py)
- **Taught on:** [Interrupt while waiting](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/tutorials/interruptions/#interrupt-a-task)

**Interrupt during service**: A task is interrupted while it holds a resource, and resumes, restarts or abandons its work.

API details

- **SimPy:** `simpy.Process.interrupt` while the process holds a unit
- **YAML:** `on_interrupt: resume`, `restart` or `abandon`
- **Builder:** `@app.task(on_interrupt=...)`
- **Low-level:** `except simpy.Interrupt`, then request again
- **Checks:** [`test_c3_interrupt_during_service`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c3_interrupts.py), [`test_c3_two_interrupts_at_one_instant`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c3_interrupts.py)
- **Taught on:** [Interrupt during service](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/tutorials/interruptions/#resume-restart-or-abandon)

**Priority preemption**: A more urgent request takes a resource unit away from a less urgent user, who is interrupted.

API details

- **SimPy:** `simpy.resources.resource.PreemptiveResource`
- **YAML:** `resources.<name>.preempt: true` with `queue: priority`; `preempt: false` on a task opts out
- **Builder:** `add_resource(..., queue="priority", preempt=True)`
- **Low-level:** `DynamicResource(..., queue="priority", preempt=True)` and `request(priority, preempt=True)`
- **Checks:** [`test_c3_priority_preemption`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c3_interrupts.py), [`test_c3_priority_preemption_equal_priorities`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c3_interrupts.py), [`test_c3_two_preemptions_at_one_instant`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c3_interrupts.py), [`test_c3_preemption_tie_between_users`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c3_interrupts.py), [`test_c3_priority_preemption_low_level`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c3_interrupts.py)
- **Taught on:** [Priority preemption](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/resources/#preemption)

## C4: Resources

Requesting and releasing resource units, in order of arrival or of priority, cancelling a request before or after its grant, and holding several resources at once.

**Ordinary request and release**: A task takes one unit of a resource, such as a packer, waits in line if none is free, and gives it back when done.

API details

- **SimPy:** `simpy.resources.resource.Resource`
- **YAML:** `resource: packers` on a task
- **Builder:** `@app.task(resource_id="packers")`
- **Low-level:** `with packers.request() as req: yield req`
- **Checks:** [`test_c4_ordinary_request_and_release`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c4_resources.py)
- **Taught on:** [Ordinary request and release](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/resources/#declare-a-resource)

**Priority request**: Waiting requests are served by priority, the lowest number first, instead of in order of arrival.

API details

- **SimPy:** `simpy.resources.resource.PriorityResource`
- **YAML:** `queue: priority` on the resource and `priority` on a task
- **Builder:** `add_resource(..., queue="priority")` and `@app.task(priority=...)`
- **Low-level:** `DynamicResource(..., queue="priority")` and `request(priority=...)`
- **Checks:** [`test_c4_priority_resource_request`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c4_resources.py), [`test_c4_priority_request_with_mixed_preempt_flags`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c4_resources.py)
- **Difference:** Equal priorities are served first in, first out, as in SimPy; desflow also offers `fifo` and `lifo` queues, under which a request's priority is ignored.
- **Taught on:** [Priority request](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/resources/#task-priority)

**Cancel before a grant**: A task leaves the queue before it is served, so it never takes a unit.

API details

- **SimPy:** `Request.cancel()` before it is granted
- **YAML:** `patience`, or an interrupt with `on_interrupt: abandon`
- **Builder:** the same
- **Low-level:** `request.cancel()`, or leaving the `with` block
- **Checks:** [`test_c4_cancel_before_a_grant`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c4_resources.py), [`test_c4_renege_ahead_of_a_preempting_request`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c4_resources.py)
- **Taught on:** [Cancel before a grant](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/resources/#cancel-and-release)

**Cancel after a grant**: A task that already holds a unit stops early and gives the unit back.

API details

- **SimPy:** `Request.cancel()` after the grant releases nothing; `Resource.release(request)` does
- **YAML:** an interrupt with `on_interrupt: abandon` gives the unit back
- **Builder:** the same
- **Low-level:** `request.cancel()` releases nothing; `resource.release(request)`
- **Checks:** [`test_c4_cancel_after_a_grant`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c4_resources.py)
- **Taught on:** [Cancel after a grant](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/resources/#cancel-and-release)

**Hold several resources**: A task holds more than one resource at once, taken in a fixed order, and can hand them to the next task.

API details

- **SimPy:** nested requests, each held while the next is awaited
- **YAML:** `resource: [picker, bench]`, acquired in that order; `keep` hands units to the next task
- **Builder:** `@app.task(resource_id=["picker", "bench"], keep=[...])`
- **Low-level:** nested `with` blocks
- **Checks:** [`test_c4_hold_several_resources`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c4_resources.py), [`test_c4_keep_hands_a_unit_to_the_next_task`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c4_resources.py)
- **Difference:** A model whose tasks acquire two resources in opposite orders is refused when it is built, because those tasks could each wait for ever; SimPy runs it.
- **Taught on:** [Hold several resources](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/resources/#several-resources)

## C5: Stores and Containers

Putting and getting items in a store and amounts in a container, with capacity limits, priority items, filtered gets, cancelled puts and gets, and the order of puts and gets at the same time.

**Bounded store put**: A task adds an item to a store, and waits when the store is full.

API details

- **SimPy:** `simpy.resources.store.Store.put`
- **YAML:** `put: {store: parcels}` on a task
- **Builder:** `@app.task(put={"store": "parcels"})`
- **Low-level:** `yield parcels.put(item)`
- **Checks:** [`test_c5_bounded_store_put`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c5_bounded.py)
- **Taught on:** [Bounded store put](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/stores-and-containers/#take-and-add)

**Bounded store get**: A task takes an item from a store, and waits when the store is empty.

API details

- **SimPy:** `simpy.resources.store.Store.get`
- **YAML:** `get: {store: parcels}` on a task
- **Builder:** `@app.task(get={"store": "parcels"})`
- **Low-level:** `item = yield parcels.get()`
- **Checks:** [`test_c5_bounded_store_get`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c5_bounded.py)
- **Taught on:** [Bounded store get](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/stores-and-containers/#take-and-add)

**Equal-time puts and gets**: When items are added and taken at the same moment, waiting tasks are served in the same order as in SimPy.

API details

- **SimPy:** `simpy.resources.store.Store`, one waiting get granted per trigger
- **YAML:** `get: {store: parcels}` and `put: {store: parcels}` on tasks
- **Builder:** `@app.task(get={"store": "parcels"})`
- **Low-level:** `yield parcels.put(item)`, `item = yield parcels.get()`
- **Checks:** [`test_c5_equal_time_puts_and_gets_follow_simpy_store`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c5_store_order.py), [`test_c5_equal_time_puts_and_gets_as_tasks`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c5_store_order.py)
- **Difference:** While a get with a filter waits, the store grants as SimPy's `FilterStore` does, looking at every waiting get each time.
- **Taught on:** [Equal-time puts and gets](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/stores-and-containers/#take-and-add)

**Bounded quantity put**: A task adds an amount to a container, such as boxes to stock, and waits when there is no room.

API details

- **SimPy:** `simpy.resources.container.Container.put`
- **YAML:** `put: {container: stock, amount: 2}` on a task
- **Builder:** `@app.task(put={"container": "stock", "amount": 2})`
- **Low-level:** `yield stock.put(2)`
- **Checks:** [`test_c5_bounded_quantity_put`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c5_bounded.py)
- **Taught on:** [Bounded quantity put](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/tutorials/stock/#take-and-restock)

**Bounded quantity get**: A task takes an amount from a container, and waits until there is enough.

API details

- **SimPy:** `simpy.resources.container.Container.get`
- **YAML:** `get: {container: stock, amount: 1}` on a task
- **Builder:** `@app.task(get={"container": "stock", "amount": 1})`
- **Low-level:** `yield stock.get(1)`
- **Checks:** [`test_c5_bounded_quantity_get`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c5_bounded.py)
- **Taught on:** [Bounded quantity get](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/tutorials/stock/#take-and-restock)

**Priority item storage**: Items in a store come out by priority, the lowest number first, instead of in the order they went in.

API details

- **SimPy:** `simpy.resources.store.PriorityStore`
- **YAML:** `stores.<name>.priority: true` and a `put` with `priority`
- **Builder:** `add_store(..., priority=True)` and `put={"store": ..., "priority": ...}`
- **Low-level:** `DynamicStore(..., priority=True)` with `simpy.PriorityItem`
- **Checks:** [`test_c5_priority_item_storage`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c5_priority_store.py)
- **Difference:** Equal priorities come out in put order in the builder and YAML, which add a rising put order to the priority; a plain SimPy `PriorityStore` gives no order among equal priorities.
- **Taught on:** [Priority item storage](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/stores-and-containers/#start-with-items-and-serve-by-priority)

**Filtered retrieval**: A task takes only an item that matches a condition, such as a parcel for its own area.

API details

- **SimPy:** `simpy.resources.store.FilterStore.get(filter)`
- **YAML:** `get: {store: parcels, filter: item.area == attr.area}`
- **Builder:** `get={"store": "parcels", "filter": ...}`, a condition or a function of the item
- **Low-level:** `parcels.get(filter=lambda item: ...)`
- **Checks:** [`test_c5_filtered_retrieval`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c5_inventory.py)
- **Difference:** A priority store takes no filter, because SimPy has no store that both ranks and filters.
- **Taught on:** [Filtered retrieval](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/stores-and-containers/#pick-an-item-or-give-up-waiting)

**Cancel store get**: A task stops waiting for an item, for example when its patience runs out.

API details

- **SimPy:** `simpy.resources.base.Get.cancel()`
- **YAML:** `patience` on a task with a store `get`
- **Builder:** `@app.task(get={"store": ...}, patience=...)`
- **Low-level:** `get.cancel()`
- **Checks:** [`test_c5_cancel_store_get`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c5_inventory.py)
- **Taught on:** [Cancel store get](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/stores-and-containers/#pick-an-item-or-give-up-waiting)

**Cancel quantity get**: A task stops waiting for an amount from a container.

API details

- **SimPy:** `simpy.resources.base.Get.cancel()`
- **YAML:** `patience` on a task with a container `get`
- **Builder:** `@app.task(get={"container": ...}, patience=...)`
- **Low-level:** `get.cancel()`
- **Checks:** [`test_c5_cancel_quantity_get`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c5_inventory.py)
- **Taught on:** [Cancel quantity get](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/stores-and-containers/#pick-an-item-or-give-up-waiting)

**Cancel store put**: A task stops waiting for room in a full store.

API details

- **SimPy:** `simpy.resources.base.Put.cancel()`
- **YAML:** an interrupt with `on_interrupt: abandon` while the put waits
- **Builder:** the same
- **Low-level:** `put.cancel()`
- **Checks:** [`test_c5_cancel_store_put`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c5_inventory.py)
- **Taught on:** [Cancel store put](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/stores-and-containers/#pick-an-item-or-give-up-waiting)

**Cancel quantity put**: A task stops waiting for room in a full container.

API details

- **SimPy:** `simpy.resources.base.Put.cancel()`
- **YAML:** an interrupt with `on_interrupt: abandon` while the put waits
- **Builder:** the same
- **Low-level:** `put.cancel()`
- **Checks:** [`test_c5_cancel_quantity_put`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c5_inventory.py)
- **Taught on:** [Cancel quantity put](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/stores-and-containers/#pick-an-item-or-give-up-waiting)

## C6: Run Control

Starting a run from a given time and state, ending it at a time, at an event or on a condition, draining it, and stepping through it one event at a time.

**Initial time**: The simulation clock starts at a given time instead of 0.

API details

- **SimPy:** `simpy.core.Environment(initial_time=...)`
- **YAML:** `simulation.initial_time`
- **Builder:** `SimulationContext(..., initial_time=100)`
- **Low-level:** `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment(initial_time=100)`
- **Checks:** [`test_c6_initial_time`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c6_run_control.py)
- **Taught on:** [Initial time](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/#initial-time)

**Initial resources**: Each resource starts with a given number of units.

API details

- **SimPy:** `simpy.resources.resource.Resource(capacity=...)`
- **YAML:** `resources.<name>.current_cap`
- **Builder:** `add_resource(name, current_cap=2, ...)`
- **Low-level:** `CapacityConfig(current_cap=2, ...)`
- **Checks:** [`test_c6_initial_resources`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c6_initial_state.py)
- **Taught on:** [Initial resources](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/#initial-time)

**Initial inventory**: Containers start with a given level, and stores with given items.

API details

- **SimPy:** `Container(init=...)`; items in a `Store`
- **YAML:** `containers.<name>.level` and `stores.<name>.items`
- **Builder:** `add_container(..., level=6)` and `add_store(..., items=[...])`
- **Low-level:** `ContainerConfig(level=6)` and `DynamicStore(..., items=[...])`
- **Checks:** [`test_c6_initial_inventory`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c6_initial_state.py)
- **Taught on:** [Initial inventory](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/stores-and-containers/#start-with-items-and-serve-by-priority)

**Initial entity state**: Each arriving entity, such as an order, starts with given attributes.

API details

- **SimPy:** the attributes a process starts with
- **YAML:** `arrivals.<name>.attributes`
- **Builder:** `add_arrival(..., attributes={...})`
- **Low-level:** the values a process is started with
- **Checks:** [`test_c6_initial_entity_state`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c6_initial_state.py)
- **Taught on:** [Initial entity state](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/task-flow/#attributes)

**Stop at a time**: The run ends at a given simulation time.

API details

- **SimPy:** `simpy.core.Environment.run(until=...)`
- **YAML:** `run.until`
- **Builder:** `app.run(until=...)`
- **Low-level:** `env.run(until=...)`
- **Checks:** [`test_c6_stop_at_a_time`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c6_run_control.py)
- **Taught on:** [Stop at a time](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/#run-length)

**Stop at an event**: The run ends when a given event happens, such as a closing signal, even before its end time.

API details

- **SimPy:** `simpy.core.Environment.run(until=event)`
- **YAML:** `run.stop: {signal: closing}` beside `run.until`
- **Builder:** `app.run(until=..., stop={"signal": "closing"})`, a signal's name, or a function returning an event
- **Low-level:** `env.run(until=event)`
- **Checks:** [`test_c6_stop_at_an_event`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c6_end_conditions.py), [`test_c6_stop_at_an_event_at_the_same_instant_as_until`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c6_end_conditions.py)
- **Difference:** When the stop and `until` fall at the same time, `until` ends the run first, as SimPy's own `until` would.
- **Taught on:** [Stop at an event](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/#stop-early)

**Explicit stop condition**: The run ends as soon as a condition on the model's state holds.

API details

- **SimPy:** `env.run(until=event)` with a process that succeeds the event when the condition holds
- **YAML:** `run.stop: {condition: level.stock >= 5}`
- **Builder:** `app.run(until=..., stop={"condition": "..."})`
- **Low-level:** `env.watch_changes(check)` and `env.run(until=event)`
- **Checks:** [`test_c6_explicit_stop_condition`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c6_end_conditions.py)
- **Taught on:** [Explicit stop condition](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/#stop-early)

**Stop arrivals and drain**: New arrivals stop, and the run goes on until everything already in the model has finished.

API details

- **SimPy:** interrupt the source, then `env.run(until=env.all_of(entities))`
- **YAML:** `run.drain: true` or `{limit: 1 h}`; `desflow run --drain`
- **Builder:** `app.run(until=..., drain=True)`, or `context.stop_arrivals()`
- **Low-level:** `source.interrupt()`, then `env.run(until=env.all_of(processes))`
- **Checks:** [`test_c6_stop_arrivals_and_drain`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c6_end_conditions.py), [`test_c6_stop_arrivals_and_drain_with_a_limit`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c6_end_conditions.py)
- **Taught on:** [Stop arrivals and drain](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/#drain)

**Step one event**: The run advances one event at a time, so a script can watch each step.

API details

- **SimPy:** `simpy.core.Environment.step()`
- **YAML:** `SimulationContext.from_yaml(path).start()`, then `.step()`
- **Builder:** `app.start()`, `app.step()`, `app.close()`
- **Low-level:** `env.step()`
- **Checks:** [`test_c6_step_one_event`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c6_end_conditions.py)
- **Difference:** A blueprint has no stepping key; its context, from `from_yaml`, steps as a builder context does.
- **Taught on:** [Step one event](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/#step-and-peek)

**Inspect next event time**: A script reads when the next event will happen without running it.

API details

- **SimPy:** `simpy.core.Environment.peek()`
- **YAML:** `SimulationContext.from_yaml(path).start()`, then `.peek()`
- **Builder:** `app.peek()`
- **Low-level:** `env.peek()`
- **Checks:** [`test_c6_inspect_next_event_time`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c6_end_conditions.py)
- **Taught on:** [Inspect next event time](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/#step-and-peek)

## C7: Patience

Customers who give up after waiting too long (reneging) and customers who do not join a queue that is too long (balking).

**Reneging**: A customer leaves the queue after waiting longer than their patience.

API details

- **SimPy:** `simpy.events.AnyOf` of a request and a timeout
- **YAML:** `patience: 3 min` on a task
- **Builder:** `@app.task(..., patience=180)`
- **Low-level:** `yield req | env.timeout(patience)`, then `req.triggered`
- **Checks:** [`test_c7_reneging`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c7_patience.py), [`test_c7_reneging_tie_timeout_scheduled_after_the_grant`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c7_patience.py), [`test_c7_reneging_tie_timeout_scheduled_before_the_grant`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c7_patience.py), [`test_c7_reneged_request_leaves_the_queue`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c7_patience.py), [`test_c7_patience_pauses_during_service`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c7_patience.py)
- **Taught on:** [Reneging](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/tutorials/patience/#leave-after-a-wait)

**Balking**: A customer does not join the queue at all when a condition holds, such as the queue being too long.

API details

- **SimPy:** a check before `Resource.request`
- **YAML:** `balk: <condition>` on a task
- **Builder:** `@app.task(..., balk="...")`
- **Low-level:** an `if` before the request
- **Checks:** [`test_c7_balking`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_c7_patience.py)
- **Taught on:** [Balking](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/tutorials/patience/#refuse-to-join)

## S1: Breakdowns

A resource that fails and is repaired, with the work it interrupts.

**Breakdown and repair**: A resource fails from time to time and is repaired, interrupting the work it was doing.

API details

- **SimPy:** a repair process holding the machine on a `PreemptiveResource`
- **YAML:** `resources.<name>.breakdown: {time_to_failure, repair, work}`
- **Builder:** `add_breakdown(resource, time_to_failure={...}, repair={...}, work=...)`
- **Low-level:** `run_breakdowns(env, resource, sampler, work=...)`
- **Checks:** [`test_s1_failure_during_service`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_s1_breakdowns.py), [`test_s1_failure_during_service_work_finishes`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_s1_breakdowns.py), [`test_s1_planned_change_during_repair`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_s1_breakdowns.py)
- **Difference:** The resource is down on a calendar clock, from the failure to the repair, even while it waits for the work in service to finish with `work: finish`.
- **Taught on:** [Breakdown and repair](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/guides/breakdowns/#steps)

## S2: Schedules

A schedule of times at which an arrival rate or a capacity changes during a run.

**Finite schedules**: Arrival rates or capacities change at set times during the run.

API details

- **SimPy:** a process that changes values at set times, started before the others
- **YAML:** `scenario` steps with `at`, `path` and `value`
- **Builder:** `add_scenario(steps)` or `add_step(at, path=..., value=...)`
- **Low-level:** `run_scenario(env, steps, until=...)`
- **Checks:** [`test_s2_step_at_an_arrival_time`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_s2_schedules.py)
- **Difference:** A step applies before every other event at its time, so the arrival gap drawn then uses the new value.
- **Taught on:** [Finite schedules](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/guides/time-varying-arrivals/#boundaries)

## S3: Replay

Arrivals read from a local CSV or Parquet file instead of drawn at random.

**Local replay**: Arrivals come from rows in a local CSV or Parquet file instead of a random distribution.

API details

- **SimPy:** a loop over recorded rows, each a timeout to its time
- **YAML:** `arrivals.<name>.replay: {path, time, unit, fields, on_invalid}`
- **Builder:** `add_arrival_replay(name, source, ...)`
- **Low-level:** `read_trace(source, ...)` and a SimPy loop over its rows
- **Checks:** [`test_s3_replay_equal_times_invalid_rows_and_the_horizon`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/main/tests/conformance/test_s3_replay.py)
- **Taught on:** [Local replay](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/tutorials/local-replay/#replay-the-rows)

## Not Yet

These features are not yet native and checked in all three APIs. "Exists" marks an API that has a form, which no conformance test compares with SimPy yet, and "checked" one that a test in the Checks column compares already; the low-level API is SimPy, so many work there already.

| Feature                                    | SimPy                                                      | YAML    | Builder | Low-level | Checks                                                                                                                             | Release |
| ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | ------- | --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| Current time                               | `core.Environment.now`                                     | exists  | exists  | exists    | none                                                                                                                               | 0.23.0  |
| Active process                             | `core.Environment.active_process`                          | not yet | not yet | exists    | none                                                                                                                               | 0.23.0  |

## Differences Kept by Design

- **A run with no until** (SimPy: `core.Environment.run()` returns when no event is left): A run with a sink or an ingress connector and no `until` runs for ever, because a live run has no end: the connectors keep events coming. Give it an `until`, with a `drain` when it should finish its work, or a `stop` that is sure to happen, or stop it with Ctrl+C.
- **Capacity 0** (SimPy: `resources.resource.Resource(capacity=0)` raises `ValueError`, and so do `Store` and `Container`): A resource, store or container may have a capacity of 0, at the start or later, because its capacity changes during a run: a shift with no packers, a shelf that is closed. At capacity 0 a resource grants no request, and a store or container accepts no put, until the capacity rises; a get still takes what a store or container holds.

# Cheat Sheet

The common YAML keys and builder calls side by side, each linked to the page that explains it. [YAML Format](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/reference/yaml-format/index.md) lists every key, and the [API Reference](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/api/index.md) every call. In the builder column, `app` is a `SimulationContext`, and a task's settings are arguments of `@app.task(...)`.

## Simulation

| To                                             | YAML                                        | Builder                                            | Read                                                                                                 |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Name the model and set the clock               | `simulation: {sim_id, factor, random_seed}` | `SimulationContext(sim_id, factor=, random_seed=)` | [Time and Pacing](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/index.md)            |
| Leave the start of a run out of the statistics | `simulation.warmup`                         | `SimulationContext(warmup=)`                       | [Statistics](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/statistics/index.md)                      |
| Start the clock at a time other than 0         | `simulation.initial_time`                   | `SimulationContext(initial_time=)`                 | [Time and Pacing](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/#initial-time)       |
| Write timestamps in a time zone                | `simulation.timezone`                       | `SimulationContext(timezone=)`                     | [Records and Telemetry](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/reference/records-and-telemetry/index.md) |

## Arrivals and Services

| To                          | YAML                                                              | Builder                                                                         | Read                                                                                                  |
| --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Draw a service time         | `services: {packing: {dist: normal, mean: 3, std: 0.5}}`          | `app.add_service("packing", dist="normal", mean=3, std=0.5)`                    | [Arrivals and Services](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/arrivals-and-services/index.md) |
| Start a task at random gaps | `arrivals: {orders: {dist: exponential, rate: 0.5, spawn: pack}}` | `app.add_arrival("orders", dist="exponential", rate=0.5)` and an `arrival_loop` | [Arrivals and Services](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/arrivals-and-services/index.md) |
| Give each entity attributes | `arrivals.<name>.attributes`                                      | `app.add_arrival(..., attributes={...})`                                        | [Task Flow](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/task-flow/index.md)                         |
| Replay recorded arrivals    | `arrivals.<name>.replay: {path, time}`                            | `app.add_arrival_replay(name, source)`                                          | [Local Replay](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/tutorials/local-replay/index.md)                    |
| Fit a service time to data  | `desflow fit`, then `!include`                                    | `fit_column(values)`                                                            | [Input Fitting](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/input-fitting/index.md)                 |

## Resources, Stores and Containers

# About

# Roadmap

Releases come in the order shown, without dates: a release ships when it is ready. The timeline lists released work, marked with a tick, then the work planned for the coming releases, in order, marked with a clock. Each item links to its GitHub issue.

## Now and next

Rename to desflow

Done in 0.20.0: the package, its import name and its command are all `desflow`. The old `dynamic-des` names still work, with a warning, until a later release.

Distributions and seeds

Done in 0.21.0: more distributions, including `empirical`, which draws from values measured in a real system. Each distribution draws from its own random stream, so adding an arrival leaves the other draws unchanged. desflow now needs Python 3.11 or later. [#42](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/42)

Ingress messages

Done in 0.21.0: every ingress connector, Kafka, Redis and PostgreSQL, takes a parameter change as `path` and `value`, the names a scenario step already uses. [#51](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/51)

Stores, containers and priority

Done in 0.21.0: tasks take items from stores and amounts from containers, and a resource serves its queue oldest first, newest first or by task priority. [#43](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/43)

Flows

Done in 0.21.0: routing between tasks by a condition or by probability, entity state that an order keeps from task to task, and delays without a resource. [#44](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/44)

Statistics and ground truth

Done in 0.21.0: wait and service times, throughput, utilisation and queue length as telemetry, with a warm-up period; and ground-truth records of what a scenario changed, so a detector or an agent can be scored against them. [#45](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/45)

Native core parity

Done in 0.22.0: the operations on the SimPy Compatibility page, natively in YAML, the builder and the low-level API, each checked against SimPy: signals, interrupts, tasks needing several resources, filtered store gets, stopping and stepping a run, and customers who give up on a queue or never join it. [#64](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/64)

Breakdowns, changing demand and replay

Done in 0.22.0: a resource that fails and is repaired, a schedule of times at which an arrival rate or a capacity changes, and arrivals read from a local CSV or Parquet file. [#65](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/65)

Replications

Done in 0.22.0: run a model with many seeds and get each statistic with a confidence interval, so a result is never read from one run. [#59](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/59)

Experiments

Done in 0.22.0: compare designs and sweep parameters over replications, fail an experiment when a result breaks a limit, fit a distribution to measured data, and write a Markdown report, all on one machine. [#66](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/66)

Speed

Done in 0.22.0: faster runs that publish the same records. [#24](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/24)

Record contract

Done in 0.22.0: every record field documented with its type and format, payload keys such as `__table__` reserved for desflow, a `timezone` setting for timestamps, and no `lag_seconds` from a run at full speed. The format is frozen before 1.0. [#51](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/51)

SimPy parity

In 0.23.0: every SimPy 4.1.2 feature natively in YAML, the builder and the low-level API, each checked against SimPy, such as nested conditions, event callbacks, unlimited stores and custom resource types. The SimPy Compatibility page lists each one, and the two differences kept by design. [#71](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/71)

Blueprint schema and AI skill

A JSON Schema for blueprints, shipped in the package, so editors complete keys and flag mistakes as you type, and a skill that teaches an AI assistant to write and check blueprints. [#41](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/41)

Downstream checks

With the blueprint schema: before a release, the tests of projects that use desflow, the benchtop data generators, run against the new version, and a test fails when a public class, function or argument is removed or changed. [#67](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/67)

desflow explain

Shows a simulation as a graph, marks each resource OK, congested or unstable (its queue grows without limit), names the bottleneck and suggests changes. `desflow run --sample` prints a few records from a blueprint. [#47](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/47)

Learn section

The shop tutorial, which extends one shop model page by page and answers a question with a number on each page, has 20 pages since 0.22.0, which added replications, comparing designs, sweeps, fitting, patience, interruptions, end conditions and more. Left: concept pages on a simulation study, checking and validating, queueing and output analysis, a final study of the whole shop and an independent problem. [#60](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/60)

## Later

The work after the Learn section, on the way to 1.0, in the order it is planned.

- **Storage and Python 3.15**

  ______________________________________________________________________

  Parquet and JSONL on more cloud storage, more Iceberg catalogs, and Python 3.15 support.

  [#32](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/32), [#40](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/40)

- **Library hooks for the server**

  ______________________________________________________________________

  Changes the server will need, made before 1.0 so the server adds to the library without changing it: parameter changes that report who made them and why, and a way to load and inspect a simulation folder.

  [#70](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/70)

- **Reserve the gen key**

  ______________________________________________________________________

  Before 1.0, a blueprint refuses a mapping with a `gen` key in a payload, a scenario value, a `record` field, a task's `set` or an arrival's `attributes`. After 1.0, `gen` marks a generated value, such as `{gen: uniform, ...}`, so no 1.0 blueprint can already use the key for something else.

  [#53](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/53)

- **Record contract freeze**

  ______________________________________________________________________

  A final check of every record field, then the format is marked frozen: no 1.x release removes a field, renames it or changes its type.

  [#51](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/51)

- **1.0**

  ______________________________________________________________________

  The generated YAML key reference, a command-line page, a compatibility policy and upgrade notes.

  [#54](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/54)

## What 1.0 means

From 1.0, the YAML blueprint format, the `desflow` command, the public Python API (`SimulationContext`, `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment` and the connectors) and the published record format stay compatible across every 1.x release. The package status moves from Beta to Production/Stable.

## After 1.0

### Simulation model

- **Maintenance, schedules and incidents:** planned maintenance, a failure clock that runs only while a resource works, schedules that repeat by time of day, and incidents that change several parameters at once. 0.22.0 ships random breakdowns with repair and finite schedules.
- **More flow and resource features:** batching, matching and splitting, setup times, and resources chosen by skill.
- **Reuse, costs and continuous flow:** parts of a model defined once and used several times, costs and energy per resource state, and levels that rise and fall continuously.
- **Transport on maps:** vehicles that move between locations on real roads and publish their positions.
- **Data-driven inputs:** arrivals replayed from a database, or taken live from a Kafka topic.
- **Decisions from outside:** a dispatcher or an agent answers for one order or session, and a run can repeat exactly from a log of those answers.

### Analysis

- **Experiments:** experiment designs, optimisation, and calibration against observed data.
- **Fitting and comparison:** distribution fitting from more data sources, automatic fault-impact experiments, and fuller run comparison and fidelity scoring.

### Simulation server

The server ships after 1.0, as 1.x releases installed with the `server` extra.

- **Server API and MCP tools:** `desflow serve` runs simulations through a REST API: upload, start, stop, change parameters during a run and follow its events. MCP tools, which let an AI agent do the same, are experimental. ([#48](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/48))
- **Browser UI:** the same from a browser, including each simulation's graph from `desflow explain`. ([#49](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/49))
- **Schedules:** run simulations on cron schedules. ([#50](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/50))
- **Server image and odctl profile:** a published image and an [odctl](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/odctl) profile run the server locally with nothing installed on the host. ([#52](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/52))
- **Visualisation:** animation of a running or recorded simulation, and a map view.
- **Distributed runs:** workers on several machines.

### Writing simulations

- **Generated values in blueprints:** random values, IDs and timestamps in YAML, then entities, relations between records, states and ramps.
- **Preview loop:** run a blueprint again each time the file changes, and check a file without running it.
- **Example gallery and visual builder.**
- **Conversion:** turn a YAML blueprint into builder code, and builder code into YAML with no Python, with an error that names each part that cannot be converted and how to rewrite it.

### Connectors

- **More sinks:** a webhook sink, a generic SQL sink and more.
- **Delivery faults:** records delivered late, twice, damaged or not at all, to test how a pipeline handles them.
- **Lineage:** each run reported to OpenLineage and OpenMetadata.

### Platform

- **More speed:** cheaper record publishing, which takes about 40 percent of a run, with the same published records ([#69](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/69)), and a faster runtime for YAML-only blueprints if measurements show the need.

### Docs

- **Reference:** a page for each generator and connector, with examples and the records they produce, and a command-line cheat sheet.
- **How-To:** generating data at scale, and testing pipelines with simulated data.

# Changelog

Each release, newest first: what changed, then under Upgrading what to change in code, commands or installs that use the previous release.

## Version 0.22.0

The low-level API is SimPy, with desflow's own resources, stores and containers, so SimPy code runs there. The SimPy Compatibility page lists every modelling feature of SimPy 4.1.2 with its status in each API: 48 are native in YAML, the builder and the low-level API and checked against plain SimPy, 48 are not yet, which 0.23.0 makes native, as the [Roadmap](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/about/roadmap/index.md) says, and 2 are differences kept by design.

- A [SimPy Compatibility](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/reference/simpy-compatibility/index.md) page lists every SimPy 4.1.2 modelling feature with its status in each API, its forms and the tests that compare it with SimPy.
- Patience and balking: a task's `patience` takes a duration such as `30 s`, and orders that leave or refuse to join are counted as `tasks.<task>.reneged` and `.balked`. See [Patience](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/tutorials/patience/index.md) and [Reneging and Balking](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/guides/reneging-and-balking/index.md).
- A store can start with items: `stores.<name>.items`, `add_store(..., items=[...])` and `DynamicStore(..., items=[...])`; a priority store takes `[priority, item]` pairs. `initial_time` takes a duration such as `8 h`. See [Stores and Containers](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/stores-and-containers/#start-with-items-and-serve-by-priority) and [Time and Pacing](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/#initial-time).
- A store `get` can take a `filter`, such as `item.area == attr.area`, and `patience` covers the wait for a `get` as well as for a resource; `item_field` adds the item a YAML get took to the payload. See [Stores and Containers](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/stores-and-containers/#pick-an-item-or-give-up-waiting) and [Filtered Inventory](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/tutorials/filtered-inventory/index.md).
- Tasks interact as SimPy processes do: `signals` that tasks fire and wait for, a `wait` for one or all of signals, child flows, timeouts and conditions, and `fail`, `fail_reason` and `on_fail` for a task that fails. `context.spawn` returns the process it starts, and `context.call` starts a child flow. See [Process Interaction](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/tutorials/process-interaction/index.md), [Tasks and Processes](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/tasks-and-processes/#wait-signals-and-child-flows) and [Wait for One or All](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/guides/wait-for-one-or-all/index.md).
- Interrupts and preemption: an `interrupt` on a task or scenario step, or `context.interrupt`, interrupts running task instances; `on_interrupt: resume`, `restart` or `abandon` says what each does; `preempt: true` on a priority resource lets a lower priority value take a busy unit. See [Interruptions](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/tutorials/interruptions/index.md) and [Resources](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/resources/#preemption).
- A task can hold several resources, `resource: [picker, bench]`, acquired in that order, and hand a unit to the next task with `keep`; a model that acquires resources in opposite orders is refused. See [Competing Resources](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/tutorials/competing-resources/index.md) and [Resources](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/resources/#several-resources).
- End conditions: `run.stop` ends a run at a signal or a condition, and `run.drain` (or `desflow run --drain`) stops the arrivals at `until` and finishes the entities already in the model; `start()`, `step()`, `peek()` and `close()` step a builder or YAML run one event at a time, and `finish()` runs a started run on to its end. The statistics count `flows.<arrival>.started` and `in_system`, and `tasks.<task>.in_progress`. See [End Conditions](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/tutorials/end-conditions/index.md) and [Time and Pacing](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/#stop-early).
- A low-level request can be cancelled with `request.cancel()` and given back with `resource.release(request)`, as in SimPy. See [Resources](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/resources/#how-it-works).
- Breakdowns: `resources.<name>.breakdown`, `add_breakdown` and `run_breakdowns` make a resource fail at random and be repaired, interrupting the work it was doing or letting it finish; each failure and repair publishes `down` and `repaired`, and the statistics count `resources.<name>.down`, `downtime` and `failures`. The Preemptive Breakdowns guide becomes [Breakdowns](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/guides/breakdowns/index.md). See also [Resources](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/resources/#breakdowns).
- Schedules in every API: the builder's `add_scenario` and `add_step`, and the low-level `run_scenario`, take the same steps as a blueprint's `scenario`. See [Time-varying Arrivals](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/guides/time-varying-arrivals/index.md) and [Changing Demand](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/tutorials/changing-demand/index.md).
- Replay: an arrival's `replay`, `add_arrival_replay` and the low-level `read_trace` take arrivals from the rows of a CSV or Parquet file, or a list of dicts, at their recorded times, with the row's fields as attributes. See [Local Replay](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/tutorials/local-replay/index.md) and [Arrivals and Services](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/arrivals-and-services/#replay).
- Faster runs at `factor: 0`: SimPy's own step processes each event, a record's timestamp is formatted once per second of the clock, and `ConsoleEgress` logs a batch with one call. A low-level workload runs 1.14 times faster than in 0.21.0, and printing every record costs about a seventh of what it did. See [Performance Tuning](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/guides/performance-tuning/index.md), whose measurements `benchmarks/throughput.py` repeats.
- `simulation.lag_interval` and `SimulationContext(lag_interval=)` set how often `system.simulation.lag_seconds` is published. See [Time and Pacing](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/#lag).
- The record contract: [Records and Telemetry](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/reference/records-and-telemetry/index.md) gives every field its type, and a docs test fails when the page and the payload models differ. `simulation.timezone`, `SimulationContext(timezone=)` and `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment(timezone=)` name the zone timestamps are written in, and [Statistics](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/statistics/#which-entities-a-count-covers) defines which entities each count covers.
- Replications: `desflow run FILE --replications N` and `desflow.replicate` run a model with seeds spawned from one seed, ending each replication at `until`, a `stop` or the end of a `drain`, and give each statistic's mean and 95% half-width; the model's sinks receive the result once, as `<sim_id>.stats.<measure>.replication.<i>`, `.mean`, `.half_width` and `.n`. See [Replications](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/replications/index.md) and [Trusting Results](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/tutorials/trusting-results/index.md).
- Experiments: `desflow experiment` and `desflow.run_experiment` compare designs with paired replications and sweeps, ending each run at `until`, a `stop` or the end of a `drain`, apply checks that fail the command, compare with observed values, and write CSV and JSON results and a `report.md`; `desflow report` builds the report again. See [Experiments](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/experiments/index.md), [Comparing Designs](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/tutorials/comparing-designs/index.md) and [Parameter Sweeps](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/tutorials/parameter-sweeps/index.md).
- Input fitting: `desflow fit` and `desflow.fit_column` fit a column of measured times to every distribution family, with diagnostics and a plot, and write settings a blueprint loads with the new `!include` tag. See [Input Fitting](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/input-fitting/index.md), [Fit the Inputs](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/tutorials/fit-the-inputs/index.md) and [Fit a Distribution](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/guides/fit-a-distribution/index.md).
- An unknown key in a blueprint or an experiment file names the closest key that place takes, such as "did you mean 'patience'?", and a misspelt name of a resource, task, signal or path names the closest one; the errors this release adds say how to fix them.
- Easier to start: the [Home](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/index.md) page has a "Where to Start" table, the [Cheat Sheet](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/reference/cheat-sheet/index.md) gives the common YAML keys and builder calls side by side, and every tutorial and How-To page gives its level: Basics, Intermediate or Advanced.

### Upgrading

- desflow needs SimPy 4.1.2 or later, where it accepted 4.0.0, and pydantic 2.6.0 or later, where it accepted 2.0.0, with which desflow 0.22.0 does not import. The conformance tests check desflow against SimPy 4.1.2, which chooses the user to preempt differently from 4.1.1 on equal keys; SimPy 4.0 also imports `pkg_resources`, which a new Python environment does not have.
- A store or container built with a capacity of 0 now works, as a resource does, and holds nothing until its capacity rises; SimPy's `ValueError` stopped it before.
- A `priority` on a store `get` is refused; priority orders a `put` into a priority store.
- Resources grant units with the same events as SimPy's `Resource`, so requests at the same simulation time are granted in SimPy's order, which can change seeded output where such ties occur.
- `patience` now covers a task's whole wait, its `wait`, its resource and its `get`, where it covered only the resource, so a task can renege while it waits for stock. It counts waiting time only, so a preempted task that queues again goes on with the time it has left. A task with `patience` needs a resource, a `get` or a `wait`.
- A store without priority is now a SimPy `FilterStore`, so a `get` can take a filter. While no waiting `get` has a filter, it grants gets as `simpy.Store` does, one waiting `get` each time it is triggered, as before; while a filtered `get` waits, it looks at every waiting `get` each time, as `FilterStore` does, so gets at the same instant can be granted in another order.
- A builder task whose function raises, or a YAML task whose `!python` payload function raises, now fails the task, publishing `failed` with the error as its reason and ending the entity's flow, instead of stopping the run.
- `DynamicResource.pool` and `DynamicResourceRequest.cancelled` are gone: the resource grants units as SimPy's `Resource` does. Call `request.cancel()` to leave the queue; `resource.queue.items` holds `(rank, request)` pairs, where it held `PriorityItem`s. A request that gives up, by `cancel()` or by reneging, now leaves the queue at once, so `len(resource.queue.items)` and the `queue_length` and `queue_length_avg` statistics no longer count it.
- The built-in statistics publish new names: `tasks.<task>.in_progress` from `minimal`, and `flows.<arrival>.started` and `in_system` from `basic`. A low-level process that calls `env.stats.task_queued`, `task_started` and `task_finished` publishes `in_progress` too, and one that calls `flow_started` publishes the flow counts.
- Events with the statuses `balked`, `reneged`, `failed`, `interrupted`, `preempted` and `resumed`, and a resource's `down` and `repaired` events, keyed by its name, reach the sinks, so a consumer that filters on `status` should expect them.
- A scenario step now applies before every other event at its time, as SimPy applies its own `until`, so an arrival at the step's time draws its next gap from the new value; seeded runs whose steps fall on the time of another event can give other numbers.
- At `factor: 0`, `system.simulation.lag_seconds` is no longer published unless `lag_interval` (low-level `lag_monitor_interval`) is set; a run that goes live publishes it from the go-live instant. At a `factor` above 0 it is published every simulation second, as before.
- `ConsoleEgress` logs each batch with one call, one line per record, so the logging format's prefix starts each batch rather than each line. Code that reads the console log record by record splits each message into lines.
- At `factor: 0`, with no `go_live_at` still to come, each event is processed by SimPy's own step and `strict=True` is not checked, as there is no wall clock to fall behind; while a `go_live_at` is pending, the real-time step runs as before.
- Every `timestamp` now carries a time zone offset, such as `2026-10-03T12:00:00.000+10:00`, so a consumer that parses it must accept `+HH:MM`, and a sink column without a zone, such as a PostgreSQL `timestamp`, now gets the UTC wall time. By default timestamps are in UTC, `+00:00`, where they were in the machine's local time with no offset; set `timezone` to an IANA name to write them in a zone. A `logical_start_time` or `go_live_at` without an offset, `now` and the default start are read in `timezone`, else in the zone of `logical_start_time`, else in UTC, not in local time: for a start or go-live of now, pass `datetime.now(timezone.utc)`, not `datetime.now()`, whose local wall time would be read in that zone and be off by the difference. `env.start_datetime` always has a time zone. A start and a go-live, one with an offset and one without, no longer fail. The clock runs in UTC, so a daylight-saving change no longer adds or drops simulation time.
- A Parquet file now has a column for every key of any row in its batch, where the first row's keys alone were written and later keys were lost; a key that first appears in a later batch adds a column to the later files, and an integer column that later gets a float becomes a double. An Iceberg table not named in `schemas` gains such a key as an optional column. A batch a Parquet or Iceberg sink cannot write is logged at ERROR, where it stopped the sink with no error.
- A container's starting level keeps its type in YAML, the builder and the low-level API, so `level: 1`, `level=1` or `init=1` gives a level of 1, as SimPy does, where it gave 1.0.
- A payload key that starts and ends with two underscores, such as `__table__`, is reserved: Kafka, Parquet, JSON Lines, Iceberg and the console drop it, with a warning, where they wrote it as data. Rename such a key, such as `__source__` to `source`, to keep it. PostgreSQL and Redis still route by `__table__` and `__stream__`. Routers, such as a Kafka `topic_router` or a storage `path_router`, no longer see the dropped keys; PostgreSQL and Redis still write any other such key as data.
- Fitting needs the new `fit` extra, which installs scipy and matplotlib: `pip install "desflow[fit]"`. The `all` extra includes it, so `desflow[all]` now installs both.
- The `glue` extra needs boto3 1.26.0 and aws-glue-schema-registry 1.0.0 or later, and the `glue` and `confluent` extras need dataclasses-avroschema 0.65.7 or later; an environment with older releases upgrades them.

## Version 0.21.0

The simulation model grows: more distributions, stores and containers that tasks use, flows of tasks, built-in statistics and ground-truth labels. The docs gain a Learn section with a tutorial, the Shop, and a User Guide with one page per part of the library.

- Five new distributions, `uniform`, `triangular`, `gamma`, `weibull` and `empirical`, and, in YAML, durations such as `5 min` for every time-valued parameter. The builder's distribution parameters take numbers in seconds, and its `warmup` and `run(until=)` also take durations; the low-level API takes numbers in seconds. See [Arrivals and Services](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/arrivals-and-services/index.md) and [Distributions](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/reference/distributions/index.md).
- Each distribution draws from a random stream of its own, so adding an arrival leaves the other draws unchanged. A run without a seed draws one and logs it, and `desflow run --seed N` repeats it. See [Randomness and Seeds](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/tutorials/randomness-and-seeds/index.md).
- Stores and containers that tasks take from and add to, with `get` and `put`; a container's `level` is a live path. See [Stores and Containers](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/stores-and-containers/index.md).
- A queue order per resource, `fifo`, `lifo` or `priority`, and a `priority` per task. See [Resources](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/resources/index.md).
- Flows of tasks: `next` by name, condition or weights, entity attributes with `attributes` and `set`, and timed steps with a service and no resource. A builder arrival loop takes a task's instance id from `context.next_instance(task)`, the counter `next` uses too. See [Task Flow](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/task-flow/index.md).
- Built-in statistics at five levels, `stats: none` to `stats: all`, and a `warmup` that leaves the start of a run out. See [Statistics](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/statistics/index.md).
- Ground-truth labels: a scenario step's `record` publishes what it changed to `when: labels` sinks only. See [Live Parameters](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/live-parameters/#record-what-a-change-was-for).
- Every ingress connector reads `path` and `value`, and a bad message is logged and skipped. See [Ingress](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/ingress/index.md).

### Upgrading

- Python 3.11 or later is needed.
- Ingress messages use `path` and `value`: Kafka's `path_id` and Redis's `param_path` and `param_value` are renamed, and a Kafka message, or a PostgreSQL ingress row, with a null `value` is now refused. Call `send_config(topic, path=..., value=...)` where it was called with `path_id=`.
- For each table the PostgreSQL ingress reads, `simulation_params` by default, rename the columns: `ALTER TABLE simulation_params RENAME COLUMN param_path TO path;` and `ALTER TABLE simulation_params RENAME COLUMN param_value TO value;`
- An event's key is now the entity's key, the arrival name and a counter from 1 (`orders-1`), not `task-<task id>`, and every event has two new fields after `key`: `task` and `instance`. PostgreSQL rows gain `task` and `instance` columns where the table has them. See [Records and Telemetry](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/reference/records-and-telemetry/index.md).
- `telemetry` entries in a blueprint no longer take `publish`. Use `stats: minimal`, which publishes the same readings as `Shop.stats.resources.<name>.<reading>`, and `function` for readings of your own.
- Seeded runs give other numbers than before, because each distribution has its own random stream, and requests of equal priority are now served first in, first out.
- A distribution parameter the family does not take, such as `rate` on a `normal`, is now refused at build. The builder's distribution parameters are keyword-only: write `add_service("packing", "normal", mean=3)`.
- Under the default `fifo` queue a request's `priority` is ignored. Add the resource with `queue="priority"` (YAML `queue: priority`; low-level `DynamicResource(env, sim_id, name, queue="priority")`) to rank requests; a task `priority` on another order is refused.
- `context.wait_for_arrival` now yields the new `Entity`. Pass it to the task as `entity=`, or the task starts an entity of its own keyed by the task's name.
- A container's `current_cap` is its capacity, its largest amount; a model that used it as a level moves to `level`. `DynamicContainer(init=None)` now starts at the registry's level, 0 unless the `ContainerConfig` gives one.

## Version 0.20.0

The package dynamic-des is renamed desflow. The classes, the YAML format, the records and the extras are the same as in 0.19.0.

### Upgrading

- Install `desflow` instead of `dynamic-des`, with the same extras: `pip install desflow`, `uv add desflow`, or for example `pip install "desflow[kafka]"`. The last dynamic-des release, 0.20.0, installs desflow with the same extras. To install desflow beside dynamic-des 0.19.0 instead, uninstall dynamic-des first: with pip, uninstalling it afterwards also removes `dynamic_des` and `ddes`, and `pip install --force-reinstall --no-deps desflow` puts them back.
- Import `desflow` instead of `dynamic_des`, for example `from desflow import SimulationContext`.
- Run the `desflow` command instead of `ddes`, for example `desflow run shop.yaml` or `desflow examples`.
- `import dynamic_des` still works in this release. It shows a `FutureWarning` and gives the desflow modules, submodules such as `dynamic_des.connectors.egress.kafka` included. The `ddes` command still works too: it prints a warning and runs `desflow`. Both are removed in a later release, which this page will name.
- The docs are at [jaehyeon.me/desflow](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/), and the repository is [jaehyeon-kim/desflow](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow) on GitHub.
